1) SNAP household: one person, age 85 and disabled, so this is an elderly/disabled (EBD) household in Wisconsin FoodShare.

   - SS survivor benefits: $12,934 / 12 = $1,077.83
   - Other survivor benefits, counted as unearned income: $10,392 / 12 = $866.00
   - Total: $2,581.83 per month.
3) Broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE). WI FSH 4.2.1 makes most food units categorically eligible when gross income is at or below 200% FPL. The FY2026 200% limit for one person (WI FSH 8.1.1, Oct 1 2025 – Sep 30 2026) is $2,610. Since $2,581.83 ≤ $2,610, the household is BBCE with no net income test and no asset test. For Oct–Dec 2026, the 2026 HHS guideline of $15,960 (published Jan 2026) gives 200% = $2,660 per month, so the household still qualifies.
4) Benefit formula (7 CFR 273.10(e); WI FSH 8.1.3 FY2026 values):
   - Earned income deduction: 20% × $638 = $127.60
   - Standard deduction (1–3 persons): $209
   - Excess medical: ($500 + $300) / 12 = $66.67, minus $35 = $31.67
   - Adjusted income: $2,581.83 − $127.60 − $209 − $31.67 = $2,213.56
   - Excess shelter: rent $600 minus half of adjusted income ($1,106.78) gives $0. No utility cost is listed, so no SUA is applied. Even with WI's $553 HSUA, the excess shelter would only be about $46, which changes nothing.
   - Net income: about $2,213.56; 30% of it is about $664.
   - Maximum allotment for one person in FY2026 is $298. $298 − $664 is below zero, so the computed benefit is $0.
5) Minimum benefit. Under 7 U.S.C. 2017(a) and 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C), eligible one- and two-person households get the minimum benefit. WI FSH 7.1.1.4 (Release 26-01, 4/15/2026) says categorically eligible one- or two-person groups get a $24 minimum, and WI FSH 8.1.1 (FY2026) also gives $24. Because the household is eligible through BBCE, it gets $24 per month instead of $0.
6) Annual amount: $24 × 12 = $288.

Why the consensus of 0 is wrong: it treats the household only under regular EBD rules (net income ≤ 100% FPL, $1,305, which it fails). It misses that gross income is just under Wisconsin's 200% FPL BBCE limit, which removes the net income test and triggers the one-person minimum benefit.

Parameter timing: FY2026 values (max $298, minimum $24, standard deduction $209, 200% FPL $2,610) were published in Aug 2025 and Dec 2025, before the freeze. FY2027 COLA values (max $306, minimum $25, effective Oct 1 2026) were not published until after 2026-07-03, so they were not part of the frozen law.

structured_output.definition_reading: This is the annual SNAP (FoodShare) benefit for the household's single SNAP unit, the 85-year-old disabled head, summed over the 12 months of 2026. Every month the household is eligible through Wisconsin's broad-based categorical eligibility because gross income ($2,581.83) is at or below 200% FPL. Its computed benefit is $0, so as a one-person household it gets the $24 minimum: $24 × 12 = $288.
structured_output.ambiguity: There is one timing question. Calendar 2026 includes Oct–Dec 2026, which falls in FY2027. USDA's FY2027 COLA raised the minimum benefit to $25, but it was published after the 2026-07-03 freeze. Using it would give 9 × $24 + 3 × $25 = $291 instead of $288. Under the frozen law, which only had the FY2026 $24 minimum, the answer is $288. A reader who ignored BBCE and applied only the regular EBD net-income test (100% FPL, $1,305) would get $0, but Wisconsin's handbook applies BBCE to EBD units at or below 200% FPL, so that reading is not supported.
